browserSourcePatches.note: Floe local frontend patch, not an upstream commit. A batched two-finger touchstart initializes the shared start/target from the first touch before entering the existing multi-touch path; retained positions from a completed gesture are discarded for the next batched birth, and touchcancel clears multiTouch.

Chained after ios-batched-touch-start.patch on the same file. onTouchCancel propagates the cancelled two-finger gesture to the current target before clearing the position/target state, so ZoomControl can close its live zoom-frame in the same gesture without committing a zoom. The native Pencil/palm gate is untouched.

Floe local frontend patch, not an upstream commit. Every two-finger move paints the existing zoom-frame at the range-clamped, unrounded target scale before the gesture ends. The end commit is synchronous in the same gesture and takes the nearest integer level to the range-clamped finger zoom (rounding step at most half a level), keeping the zoomTo guard/hook set (OverviewFade, _limitZoom, spreadsheet closePopups); the historical outward ceil/floor value is retained only as the beyond-range Overview guard input. touchcancel closes the frame at the start zoom without a commit.

Floe local frontend patch, not an upstream commit. Calc re-syncs its tile container synchronously at zoom finalization (_updateTileTwips -> applyZoom/endZoom and _restrictDocumentSize -> _onZoomRowColumns) without changing the visible frame height. The mobile/tablet keyboard-resize checks now run only when oldFrame.pY actually differs from the new frame.pY, so an unchanged-height zoom keeps its anchor instead of scrolling the previously selected cell back into view. A genuine height decrease still runs _onUpdateCursor and _scrollCellCursorIntoView; a genuine increase still restores the mobile input state. Geometry/range/clamp/layout updates, explicit cell navigation and frozen panes are untouched. Does not address the separate Word keyboard precondition and makes no Word claim.

Floe local frontend patch, not an upstream commit. A zoom (owned pinch, wheel or programmatic) is not a text-input intent: _onZoomEnd now holds the container's existing post-zoom replay scope across the zoom's own final _onUpdateCursor(null, true) instead of closing it first, so the passive cursor/overlay redraw can no longer force map.focus(true) + TextInput.focus(true) 7-42ms after an owned pinch rawend (the actual App20 call path) while caret geometry/scroll/selection redraw still runs. The replay scope and the final cursor update are fenced with try/finally: if the replay or the final cursor update throws (stale cursor, torn-down section or a failing render callback), the scope flag is always cleared so the next genuine input is not suppressed, and the original error still propagates untouched. _updateCursorAndOverlay's keyboard guard additionally checks the container's real isInZoomAnimation() (the map-free layout never fires 'zoomstart', leaving the old this._isZooming check permanently false), so a core cursor message arriving while the live zoom-frame is open cannot force focus either. The next genuine tap/edit/command reaches _updateCursorAndOverlay outside these scopes and focuses exactly as before; readonly, wizard, dialog and search guards are unchanged. Does not change zoom levels, anchors, replay contents or Calc's unchanged-height anchor fix.

Floe local frontend patch, not an upstream commit. Chained after ios-live-pinch-zoom.patch on the same file. A pinch that latched onto the document (first in-document move fixed the start distance/anchor) is consumed entirely by this owner, so its final touchend now calls e.preventDefault(): WebKit then does not synthesize the compatibility mousedown/click that the App20 trace recorded as a trusted canvas click ~27-129ms after rawend - an event that blurs the real text input mid-session and re-arms the input intent through Map click handling after a completed pinch. One-finger taps (never latched here), two-finger taps without an in-document move, gestures starting outside the document area, non-cancelable events and touchcancel keep their existing default behavior; the live-frame commit (nearest integer level) and cancel/restore paths are byte-identical. This complements, and does not replace, the passive focus preservation in ios-zoomend-focus-preservation.patch.
